note: SERDE TRANSPARENT IS WHAT KEEPS A NEWTYPE A BARE NUMBER ON THE WIRE, and a round-trip test cannot see it. The Ell retyped Fact.day to Option<WorldTime> (a struct with one private f64). The existing serde round-trip test passes identically whether the value serializes as 12.25 or as {day: 12.25}, so it was vacuous evidence for the save-format claim. Direct assertion instead: serde_json::to_string(&WorldTime::new(12.25)) must equal the string 12.25. Mutation-proven both ways -- deleting #[serde(transparent)] gives left: {\day\:12.25} right: 12.25 and the test goes red; restoring it goes green. If you wrap ANY serialized field in a newtype, add the bare-shape assertion in the same commit; otherwise the day the attribute is dropped, every saved world is silently rewritten and no artifact diff explains why.
